title: GMP Contingency vs Owner Allowance at Project Closeout
scenario_text:
The Monroe Street Office Tower tenant improvement project is approaching substantial completion. The GC (Lakefront Builders) is requesting release of remaining contingency funds as part of final payment. NovaTerra Monroe LLC is the owner. The project used a GMP contract based on AIA A133-2019.

**Procore — Monroe Street Office Tower, Budget Summary (as of Jun 20, 2026)**
Original GMP: $8,750,000 | Approved COs: $412,000 | Revised GMP: $9,162,000
Cost to date: $8,894,000 | Remaining contingency (contractor's): $268,000
Owner allowances (unspent): $185,000 (lobby finishes allowance — tenant selected less expensive option)
Retainage held: $458,100 (5%)

**iManage — Document: "Owner-GC Agreement, Monroe Street" (AIA A133-2019, modified)**
Article 6.3.2 (modified): "Savings resulting from the difference between the GMP and the actual Cost of the Work plus the Contractor's Fee shall be allocated 75% to Owner and 25% to Contractor."
Article 6.5.1 (standard): "Contingency funds are included in the GMP for the Contractor's exclusive use in covering cost increases..."
Exhibit D — Schedule of Allowances: "Lobby finishes: $185,000 allowance. Actual selections to be made by Owner. Unused portions revert to Owner."

**Shared Drive — \\ntserver\properties\monroe-street\capital-policy\**
File: "NovaTerra Capital Policy v2.8 (effective Jul 2024).pdf"
Section 5.2: "Unspent contingency on capital projects reverts to the property-level capital reserve upon project closeout."
Section 5.4: "GMP savings sharing shall not apply to owner-directed allowances."

**Outlook — Email from Lakefront Builders (Jun 18, 2026)**
From: k.sullivan@lakefrontbuilders.com
To: r.fitzgerald@novaterra.com
Subject: Monroe St — Final reconciliation and contingency release
"Rob — Per our GMP, we're requesting release of the remaining $268K contingency. As you know under 6.5.1 this is contractor's contingency and it's ours to manage. We also believe the 75/25 savings share in 6.3.2 applies to the full difference between GMP and actual cost including unused contingency. Our calculation: GMP savings = $9,162,000 - $8,894,000 = $268,000. Our share at 25% = $67,000. We'll credit you $201,000."

**Microsoft Teams — #monroe-street-tia (Jun 19, 2026, 11:32 AM)**
@k.sullivan.guest: Rob can we get alignment on the contingency calc before the closeout meeting Thursday?
@r.fitzgerald: Need to check something. The $185K in allowances shouldn't be in the savings calc.
@k.sullivan.guest: It's all within the GMP envelope per the contract
@r.fitzgerald: (typing indicator appeared, then disappeared — no message sent)

**Google Doc — "Monroe Street Closeout Punch List" (shared with Lakefront, last edited Jun 15)**
[RESOLVED COMMENT by @d.kowalski, Mar 2026]: "Make sure we separate the allowance savings from contingency in the final rec. The savings split does NOT apply to allowances per our capital policy. Catherine flagged this on the Wacker project last year and legal agreed."

**Yardi — Monroe Street Capital Tracking**
Project code: MNST-2025-TI | Budget category: Tenant Improvements
Note (entered by Catherine Brennan, Apr 2026): "Lobby allowance of $185K tracked separately per policy 5.4. Not subject to GMP savings share."
question: What is the correct final payment calculation for the contractor at project closeout?

contributor.name: Robert Fitzgerald
contributor.title: Construction & Capital Projects Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Change order management, GMP contracts, subcontractor disputes, lien waivers, substantial completion determinations

choices: No savings payment to contractor; all $268,000 reverts to NovaTerra's property-level capital reserve per Capital Policy Section 5.2, which supersedes the AIA contract terms.
GMP savings of $268,000 split 75/25: Owner receives $201,000, Contractor receives $67,000. The entire difference between revised GMP and actual cost is subject to the savings clause.

GMP savings calculated as $268,000 minus the $185,000 owner allowance = $83,000 in true contractor contingency savings, split 75/25: Owner receives $62,250, Contractor receives $20,750. The $185,000 in unspent allowances reverts entirely to Owner per Exhibit D and Capital Policy Section 5.4.

Contractor receives the full $268,000 remaining contingency because Article 6.5.1 designates it as contractor's contingency for their exclusive use, and savings sharing in 6.3.2 does not override this provision.
